title: Concurrent Holdings and Reservations of Safe Deposit Boxes
content:
A customer may rent more than one of the bank's Safe Deposit Boxes. Four counts bound how many, and each is taken before a new reservation is recorded.

## The counts

1. The count of the customer's rentals standing waitlisted, active, past due or pending drilling must be below 3.
2. The count for the size requested, taken over rentals in those same four standings, must be below the number of rentals of that size one customer may hold.
3. The count of the customer's rentals standing waitlisted must be below the number of open reservations one customer may hold.
4. A customer with a rental standing pending drilling cannot reserve another box.

The same four counts set out as a table:

| Count | Taken over | Condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The customer's rentals, all sizes together | rentals standing waitlisted, active, past due or pending drilling | below 3 |
| The customer's rentals of the size requested, reservations included | rentals standing waitlisted, active, past due or pending drilling | below the number of rentals of that size one customer may hold |
| The customer's open reservations | rentals standing waitlisted | below the number of open reservations one customer may hold |
| The customer's rentals standing pending drilling | — | none |

Each count is taken as the records stand on the day the reservation is considered.

## What settles the counts

The counts are settled by the bank's own record of the customer's box rentals and the standing of each, read for that customer before the new reservation is recorded. What the customer says about how many boxes they hold does not settle them.

## Points of judgement

A customer whose records show two rentals in the counted standings, hypothetically one active 5x10 Safe Deposit Box and one past-due 10x10 Safe Deposit Box, has an overall count of 2, which is below 3, so the first count is satisfied.

A customer whose records show three rentals in the counted standings has an overall count of 3. Three is not below 3, so the first count is not satisfied, and this holds however the three are spread across sizes and branches.

A rental that stands closed is in none of the four counted standings and so enters none of these counts.
